title: Nilo-Saharan languages - Wikipedia
text: The Nilo-Saharan languages are a proposed linguistic family consisting of around 210 Native African languages spoken by somewhere around 70 million speakers, mainly in the upper parts of the Chari and Nile rivers, including historic Nubia, north of where the two tributaries of the Nile meet.

text: Nilo-Saharan Languages are a family of 205 languages. The most common are Dholuo in Kenya and Kanuri in Nigeria with 3.5 million speakers each. The next largest, measured by number of speakers are: Kalenjin; Dinka, Lugbara; Lango; Maa; Acholi; Lendu; Ngambay...

text: Nilo-Saharan East Africans often have lighter skin tones, narrower noses, and thinner lips compared to West Africans. This can be attributed to the historical movements of different populations across the African continent and their interactions with various ethnic groups.
